2026-11-27.title: Friday of the Thirty-fourth Week in Ordinary Time
readings: I saw a new heaven and a new earth
Here God lives among his people
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away
2026-11-27.verse: Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
theo: Jesus points to the fig tree: when its leaves sprout, summer is near. So too, the signs of history should make us aware that the Kingdom of God is near. Then a sentence of astonishing authority: “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.” Only God can say that. The Word made flesh is the one thing in the universe that does not fade.

Revelation shows the last judgement: the dead, great and small, before the throne, and the books opened, including “the book of life”. Then the vision of hope: “a new heaven and a new earth… the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” The Church teaches that the universe itself will be transformed, and God will be with his people (CCC 1042–1047). Creation is not thrown away; it is made new.
outline: Ask: what will still be here in a thousand years?
Point 1 · Words that do not pass
We are judged by our works, written by grace.
A new heaven and a new earth.
live: Write one Gospel verse on a card and carry it this week.
Notice one sign of God's Kingdom growing around you today.
2026-11-27.prayer: Lord Jesus, heaven and earth will pass away, but your words remain. Write my name in the book of life, make me new by your grace, and bring me to the holy city where God dwells with his people. Amen.

quick: Christ's words outlast heaven and earth.
The dead are judged before the throne; the book of life is opened.
God will make all things new.
2026-11-27.action: Carry one Gospel verse with you this week.
2026-11-27.question: What am I building that will last?

homily: Dear friends, Jesus points to the fig tree: as soon as it sprouts leaves, you know that summer is near. So also, when you see these things taking place, you know that the kingdom of God is near (Luke 21:29–31). The events of history are signs that God's Kingdom is on its way.

Then he says a sentence of astonishing authority: heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away (Luke 21:33). Only God can say that. Mountains, empires, even the stars will fade; the Word made flesh will not.

Revelation shows the last judgement: the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and the books opened, including the book of life (Revelation 20:12). And then the vision of hope: a new heaven and a new earth, and the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband (Revelation 21:1–2). God does not throw creation away; he makes it new.

Let us build our lives on what does not pass away. Write one verse of the Gospel on a card and carry it with you this week. And look around you today for one sign that God's Kingdom is growing: a kindness, a reconciliation, a prayer answered. Amen.
kids: Children, flowers and trees fade, but Jesus' words last for ever. Learn one verse of the Bible by heart this week!

intro: Christ's words outlast the universe; the book of life is opened; God makes a new heaven and a new earth.

sub: The fig tree tells the season.
q: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
points.apply: Carry a Gospel verse with you this week.

sub: The dead stand before the throne.
q: But at that time your people shall be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book.

And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and books were opened. Also another book was opened, the book of life. And the dead were judged according to their works, as recorded in the books.
points.apply: Examine your conscience on this year's works.

sub: God creates new heavens and earth.
The new Jerusalem comes down as a bride.
q: For I am about to create new heavens and a new earth; the former things shall not be remembered or come to mind.

Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth; for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and the sea was no more. And I saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
points.apply: Care for creation in one concrete way.

concl: Build on the word that does not pass.
God is making all things new.
